intents.summary: Allocate public Terminal versions once per admitted batch, retaining release intent and existing reservations.

Terminal CI Vitest cache: restore a shard's newest saved modules across lockfile edits that leave Terminal's dependencies alone, prune entries a run did not read before saving, and log how the restore matched.
Terminal CI Vitest cache: the prune step now leaves the saved cache untouched, and warns, when it cannot find the directory the unit step wrote.

Kimi models now compact at their real context window instead of the 200k Claude Code assumes for an unknown model: K3.1 Pro gets a 262,144 window (about a 229k compaction threshold) on every plan unless you set a smaller one for the model.
Bundle libatomic with Linux headless CLI runtimes so stock Linux installs can start Node without installing libatomic1, and report sanitized missing-library diagnostics when startup fails.
Hide your offline trust-revoked sign-ins from machine pickers and list_machines, including tunnels left behind, while keeping online, current, and shared computers available.

Leased Personal Claude and Codex keys now stay on this computer when CodePress sign-in changes for the same person: a new token generation, a locally expired token (kept for up to 24 hours) and a 403 that is not about this computer or organization no longer delete them, so workers stop dying with "Not logged in". Turn off `terminal.personalLeaseKeepAcrossAuth` to restore the old behaviour.

Show Terminal tunnel computers in Settings and keep earlier sign-ins revocable under a collapsed Older sign-ins section, preserving the existing list on older backends.
Always keep This computer visible, including when it is revoked.

Leased Personal Claude and Codex keys keep renewing while CodePress's account listing is failing, and a Claude tab or worker launch renews a due leased key first (bounded by the lease request timeout), so a worker no longer starts on an expired token. A renewal that fails or times out launches on the current token and shows the error on the account.

Cleaning up a landed project's session folder no longer makes a worker relaunch or a new worktree on a busy machine fail with "Could not acquire worktree lifecycle lock": the machine-wide check for running processes in the folder now runs before the shared worktree lock is taken, not while it is held.

The kickoff's Runs on now lists your other machines wherever Auto is offered (including Chat), and Auto no longer hangs on "Auto is choosing where to run": it names its pick within seconds, or falls back to This machine after 2.5 s with a reason. Machine lists load faster and are shared between the Connect menu and the kickoff.

A stuck machine-list request no longer freezes Runs on → Your machines, Chat's Runs on and the Connect menu on their last list: the read gives up after 35 s, the list it had stays (marked stale), and the next poll reads again.
Retry transient Linux CLI delivery-ledger reads within the upload budget and name redacted publication refusals.
Show the hosting Mac's weekly subscription usage in a synced project's Orchestrator and Workers model pickers.

A Claude worker that prints "Not logged in · Please run /login" now recovers by itself: Terminal leases the person's active Personal account again and resumes the worker, or fails the worker over to another healthy account. A Personal lease whose renewal just failed or timed out is no longer waited on again by every launch for a minute.
Use one native activation rule for synced Claude and Codex accounts, preserve outside logins, and explain skipped switches on the Accounts card.
Strip macOS metadata from CLI archives and keep tar warnings outside the publisher's stdout limits.
Make both phone drawers a continuous surface under the thread card, without a seam border or card ring.
Continue here on a cloud chat or saved tab saves the restored tab's card at once, so a message typed into that chat on the web reaches the new tab instead of answering "did not answer".

The Ghostty terminal engine pilot now works on x86_64 Linux: Linux builds package the engine, and the background service keeps a copy of it, so opted-in users get Ghostty tabs instead of xterm with "unsupported runtime". The broker also counts output that arrives while a Ghostty snapshot is being taken toward its next checkpoint, instead of treating it as already checkpointed. A window that first reached a server without the engine (for example, before the background service swapped it to the new build's server) now retries the viewer engine from the new server instead of keeping the earlier failure. A Ghostty tab opened in the background no longer shows blank until the window is resized: revealing a tab repaints its last frame.
Start Orchestrators in the Terminal window when Claude or Codex needs its Team relay, and retry a host's window-bound launch refusal once in that window.

Read remote projects in complete count-based pages, retain unchanged Work and Fleet records, and immediately catch up on pending replies.

Preserve emoji pairs at text caps and normalize malformed Unicode before relaying project reads.
Make storage janitor initialization independent of target import order.
Accounts: the "Use on" picker on Personal account cards now sits clear of the usage bar and is a compact, theme-matched dropdown instead of the oversized native one.
Allow the background launcher poll cadence to be compressed for deterministic tests while retaining its production timing defaults.
Cap relayed tab output at 16 KiB of ANSI-stripped text so terminal UI redraws stay within the machine bridge reply limit.

Settings → Computers shows each computer's Terminal version and whether it is up to date, has an update ready, is downloading, restarting or needs updating by hand; `list_machines` reports the same, plus how many agents are busy on each machine.
Keep Auto kickoffs on This machine while the draft has attachments or @mentions, and restore the ranked pick when they are removed.
Add a separate Linux capacity-host CLI and root service with pinned containerd/Kata installation, owned bridge/firewall isolation, per-session VMs, preflight probes, admission and self-fencing.
Follow this computer's Claude and Codex account choices, support targeted account selection, and report account status to other approved computers.
Allow local Orchestrator composers to mention and read open chats on owned machines behind the default-off Cross-machine chat mentions organization flag.
Carry attachments and owned-machine conversation mentions with capable remote kickoffs, while preserving mixed-version fallback and shared-computer refusals.

Install a ready update on your other computers from one of them. Settings → Computers gets Update all and a per-computer Update, and the update button offers Update all my computers. Each computer restarts through the same tracked restart as Restart now, and waits until its agents are idle. Staff-only for now; agents can do the same with `terminal_update`.
Follow each computer's Muse account choice, including deferred idle switches, and report its local sign-ins and conversation restart state.
Keep synced project cloud copies current after record changes, refresh edited older pages, and preserve whole count-based pages up to the cloud upload ceiling.
Speed up Terminal CI test selection by sharing dependency graph walks across tests while preserving the selected tests and projects.

Keep my computers up to date: one setting in Settings → Computers (shown where remote update is on) makes every computer you own install a ready update by itself once its agents are idle, and one that was asleep or offline catches up when it is back. A waiting install that the host refuses after accepting it now shows as failed with the reason (for example "Needs an admin password there") instead of staying on "Waiting for its agents to finish", and asking for an idle install of an update that restarts the terminal runtime asks for your OK straight away.
Open synced conversations from their cloud copy before reading live updates when the organization's cloud-first flag is on.
Choose accounts for this computer, another approved computer, or all computers from the Accounts switcher, with reported running status and remote Muse confirmation.

Add the organization Runner pool to Settings → Computers, with pool status,
fallback policy, installation commands and explicit local join/leave controls.

Keep capacity hosts fenced and retryable after shutdown, heartbeat, VM creation, and uninstall failures; accept enrollment tokens only through environment or bounded stdin.

Accept successful empty namespace inventories during cleanup and retain creation boot fences for unrecognized RPC failures.
Keep project-sync snapshots from crashing the daemon: bound JSON string encoding, refuse oversized cloud copies locally, and halt repeatedly interrupted rows with a visible reason.
Keep cloud-copy snapshots smaller by omitting redundant settled PM streaming rows while preserving turn transcripts, thread anchors, worker events, and replay receipts for takeover.
Check the enrolled host identity before leaving a runner pool, preserving replacement enrollments when Leave was started from stale state.
Keep account reports flowing before this computer has its own account choice by omitting revision-zero outcomes.
Keep project cards and cloud copies syncing after a session snapshot is refused.
The weekly usage bars on a project homed on another Mac now say which Mac they were read from in their tooltip.

Update all and Keep my computers up to date are on for everyone, with no Feature Flags menu step. Only your own computers can be updated, restarts still wait for agents to go idle, and Keep my computers up to date stays off until you turn it on.
Carry remote kickoff chat mentions through the machine bridge and keep mentions on this machine until the receiver advertises support.
Keep the onboarding permission note visible on short laptop windows and the navigation footer reachable on smaller screens.
Resolve Orchestrator chat mentions through the base server context for local and bridged MCP kickoffs, and log discovery failure codes when a mention is refused.
Reuse content-validated formatting results to reduce CI time after source edits.

Allow capacity-host Kata QEMU sessions on arm64 hosts without a hardware PMU by removing only the unsupported `pmu=off` CPU feature during host join. Report the applied CPU features and reason in host doctor JSON.

Keep the server responsive during project sync by sharing repeated checkout inspections and bounding Git reads through the lightweight spawn host. Reuse sampled CPU topology for capacity heartbeats instead of repeatedly enumerating every processor.
Collect best-effort per-file Terminal integration profiles in server CI and reuse test daemon bundles.
Allow the claimed stable macOS CLI to publish while its desktop release is lane-staged, with both uploaded Darwin manifests required.
Allow private Linux tmpfs directories in the test-only reclaim safety guard, and provide a defaulted saver dependency for focused reclaim fixtures. Production cleanup behavior is unchanged.

Linux headless CLI releases publish again. The Linux desktop build now takes about nine minutes, which left the CLI packaging step less than its fixed 22-minute headroom inside the 30-minute job, so every release since 1.364.2 refused the linux-x64 CLI and the Linux CLI feeds stayed at 1.362.55. The build-linux job and its CLI deadline budget now both allow 45 minutes.

Keep the installed server context through bridged kickoffs so Orchestrator chat mentions and owned previews resolve their services. Give mention resolution ten seconds and stop discovery once every referenced project is found.
Let the local Orchestrator judge when a change needs a feature flag and follow the synced Feature flags preference in Settings → Agents.
Coordinate project-worker restores sharing a handoff repository so concurrent Git worktree creation cannot expose incomplete metadata to a sibling restore.
Report failed macOS CLI publication in the macOS arm64 release notice and name the correct platform in CLI failure annotations.
Allow QA to shorten the Claude CLI sign-in polling interval while retaining the two-second production default.
Allow runner-pool computers to run automation handler jobs in isolated VMs with shared capacity, bounded output, deadlines, and cancellation.
Import Claude Code, enabled plugin and Codex OAuth MCP servers as Terminal sign-ins and pick them up in running Orchestrator conversations.
Retry macOS CLI artifact downloads and transient immutable-upload failures with separate transfer deadlines, preserving the macOS upload allowance and publisher job cap.
Fail the Linux AppImage release check when an x86_64 build ships without the Ghostty engine, instead of letting every tab silently fall back to xterm.
Share worker Git result shaping with synchronous fixture execution so release tests preserve production error messages and output limits. Production callers retain the asynchronous default runner.
Browser tabs now reach local dev servers listening only on `::1`, for both the page and its HMR WebSocket, even when `localhost` resolves to IPv4 only.

Terminal now starts a fresh terminal broker when the previous one was killed without shutting down cleanly (for example by the OOM killer), instead of failing on every launch with "Broker endpoint unavailable before deadline".

Refresh an agent launch marker observed during screen rendering while its start deadline remains, preserving sampling deadlines and agent identity checks. Add optional observation hooks for deterministic verification without changing default timing or rendering.
Auto and Move's Suggested machine now rank your own Macs by live load whenever your feed, Project sync or copy-everywhere is on, and a Mac that has not reported says it is not reporting its load.
Deleting an untouched voice-started project now also retires its cloud copy, so other Macs stop listing a Synced project that no longer exists.

New Orchestrator projects and chats start Synced, and Local-only ones you never chose are adopted, whenever the cloud already accepts this Mac's cards (One agent feed, Project sync or session copy everywhere), not only with the One agent feed on.
This Mac's count in the feed's Machine filter no longer counts a synced project or chat twice when the cloud holds more copies than the feed lists, and still counts a Local-only project once.

A window opened for another machine now shows the one-feed switcher and rail, and the "waiting on you" count, when that setting is on, the same as the main window. Its rail leaves out Automations, Coordination and Evals, which cannot open there yet.
Another Mac now shows a synced project or chat as Working… when its turn or a background task starts, not only when the turn ends.
Retry brief GitHub download failures while bundling the desktop-control helper, so a transient 5xx no longer fails a release build.
A window opened for another machine now starts on the organization you picked in the main window, with the last one-feed answer, instead of your first organization with nothing cached.

Each Mac now periodically checks its synced projects and chats against the cloud's copies homed on it, and repairs a copy that never arrived or was lost, a copy whose project is gone, a copy with stale fields, and a card the cloud refused.
Terminal can now read the staff-only "Orchestrator repository kickoff" organization setting, in the app and on its server. Nothing uses it yet, so behavior is unchanged.

A local project can be started with `repositories` instead of, or beside, a Project folder. Terminal checks each one with `gh` before the kickoff claims its key, prepares a session worktree of the first and a `repos/<owner>/<name>` worktree of the others from `origin/<default>` when the project opens, and removes them when the project lands.
Apply computer account choices before due lease renewals, retry temporary activation failures after 5, 10 and 20 seconds, and catch up missed choices when the device channel reconnects.

The Orchestrator instructions editor no longer sits under the macOS window controls, can drag the window, and now follows the Orchestrator's light and dark theme, with a higher-contrast Contents list and text.
Match integration discovery guidance to the gateway: compact discovery may omit large schemas, and exact discovery returns the full schema without a size limit.

One failed remote command no longer switches this Mac's remote control off until Terminal restarts. Only a journal failure withdraws it, a writable journal restores it, and `get_terminal_diagnostics` reports why it was withdrawn. A cross-machine call refused because this Mac was briefly not offering control now reconnects, refreshes its capabilities and retries once, and when it still fails the error says nothing was sent and how to fix it.
Keep Claude account identity, scopes and plan details when uploading Personal or Team sign-ins, and explain reconnect failures when switching accounts.
Unify project transfers under Hand off… and offer This Mac and Cloud VM in the remote project's destination picker.

A home Mac that is told which replicas have mail waiting now also asks every two minutes, so a dropped wake-up cannot leave a queued reply or answer undelivered. Each delivery, and each reason an item was not delivered, is now in the log.
Let people choose all their CodePress organizations for Terminal's broker connection, keep agent credentials on that connection, and answer broker OAuth discovery probes with JSON.

The Orchestrator prompt editor now styles Markdown as you type: `##` titles are large with a divider above each section, and bold, italic, code and links are styled. The text is still plain Markdown, and the Preview button is gone.

Two Orchestrator projects started on the same checkout within about a minute of each other now both get a session worktree: the session branch name ends in the random tail of the project id instead of its timestamp prefix. Existing session trees keep the branch they are on.

Apply all-computer account choices immediately on the originating computer and show completion once online computers have switched, with faster refresh while switching and separate offline and refusal notes.

An Orchestrator started with repositories now sees them from its first turn: `list_directories` and `list_repositories` show each repository's worktree, its prompt names them, it can read them, `project_fleet_assign` with just a `repository` cuts the worker from the project's own checkout without cloning it again, and file references and Quick Open search them.

With the repository kickoff flag on, the kickoff input carries one quiet line, "In acme/web, api…", that names the GitHub repositories and the folder a new project starts in, and its menu adds, ticks and removes them. The Project folder card gives way to it; with the flag off nothing changes. A repository the sidecar refuses shows in red on the line and the brief is kept.

Make a question answered from another machine apply on the home exactly as it does when pressed there: an idle Orchestrator is started to take the answer, an option and the words typed beside it both arrive, and an answer that could not apply is reported back as refused instead of delivered.
Choose Auto, Local or Cloud for organization automations in Runner pool settings, and show automation capacity and recent runs beside sessions.

Answering or messaging another Mac's project now sends the words you typed with a picked option, and shows whether the Mac delivered it, could not apply it, or has not picked it up yet (with Send again), instead of an endless "Sending to…".
The feed rail's loading skeleton now lives in its own shared file, so the web dashboard can draw it without loading the whole rail. Nothing changes on screen.
Share CI-passed evidence reads across attachments and respect poll backoff and GitHub budget holds while preserving fresh checks before message delivery.

A message or ask answer sent from another Mac, the web or the phone while an Orchestrator is mid-turn is now read by that running turn, as if it had been typed in the home's composer, instead of waiting for the turn to end. It follows the composer's steering rules: when a model change is pending, an earlier queued message was not steered, or the provider declines, it runs as the next turn as before. A repeated delivery of the same message steers once, and answers given on the home Mac keep their own turns.

With cross-machine chat mentions on, the `@` menu groups Orchestrator and agent chats by machine (this machine first, then each other machine by name) so chats from your other Macs are no longer crowded out by this machine's, and shows "Searching your other machines…" while they load. The list stays visible while it refreshes, and opening the menu fetches it again when it is over 30 seconds old or failed.
Auto no longer rules out another machine just because it answered the folder check slowly: a late answer is kept and used on the next look, and a failed read is logged.

With the One agent feed setting on and remembered, Terminal now opens on the feed rail loading instead of drawing the classic project rail first, and a startup "not ready" answer from the local feed no longer flips the feed off and back on.
A project that changes on another device refreshes on this one's rail within about a second, instead of at its next 15-second poll.

The @ picker reaches other machines' agent tabs sooner: the lookup can answer tabs and Orchestrator chats separately, a machine whose chat discovery is slow or times out keeps showing the chats it last returned for ten minutes instead of dropping them, and repeated lookups reuse the feature-flag read and each machine's validation for a short time. Sending a message with a mention still checks everything fresh.
Read plan and design issues and merged PR descriptions over GraphQL so they remain available when the GitHub REST budget is exhausted. Batch Plan view issue reads in groups of up to 25.

Starting a project on another of your own Macs with an attachment or @mention no longer refuses when Local Cloud Runs is off and the Mac is up to date. A Mac whose version can't be read now says so instead of asking you to update it.
Keep selected Terminal CI checks focused when only full-suite planning inputs change, and improve full-suite verification with isolated test lanes.

A Mac that hosts Orchestrator projects can now stream a project's thread to a viewer on another device: it pushes each change as it happens instead of waiting to be polled, while someone is watching. Tool calls in a remote read also carry a short summary of what they ran (the command, path, pattern, url or query), so a viewer's tool rows say more than the tool's name.
Offer the agent tabs you may read on machines a teammate shared with you in the @ mention menu, grouped under `<machine> · <owner>`, and let the Orchestrator read them.
Auto routing now goes by real CPU utilisation, the share of busy time Activity Monitor shows, instead of the load average, and heartbeats carry the memory in use for each machine.

Allow handoff verification to compress progress polling while preserving the production request deadline and polling defaults.

Keep Muse credential execution injectable per switcher while preserving the native production executor and existing test project membership.

An open chat or project on another of your Macs now streams live in Terminal and on the web: the reply appears as the Mac writes it instead of at the next 3-second poll, and the project's card in the list keeps in step with what the open thread shows (working, and which questions are waiting on you). It falls back to the old polling on any problem, and against an older Mac or backend nothing changes.

Mention chats from a synced copy. Typing `@` in a project's copy on another machine offers this machine's and the home's chats, and the picks travel with the message so the home's Orchestrator can read them; a home that needs a newer Terminal says so in the menu.
Resolve the bundled agent runner and retained Orchestrator SDK dependencies from the installed CLI layout.

Runs on: each machine's row in the menu now shows that machine's real CPU, RAM and power (for example `8% CPU · 55% RAM · on power`), with a small Auto tag on the machine Auto picked and the same text on the Auto row. The usage line under the Runs on chip is gone.
Offer your other Macs in a remote project's Hand off picker and follow its Continue on request through completion or refusal.

The Mac that hosts an Orchestrator project now gives every thread entry one UTC time from a per-project clock that never goes backwards, and sends those times to every viewer. A message queued while a reply runs takes the time the Orchestrator reads it, reply text takes the time it arrived rather than the time it was saved, projects get their existing history timed once on first open, and a project moved to another Mac keeps its times. Nothing in the thread looks different yet.

Repository rules follow you to every computer. Terminal reads your organization's default rules and your own, applies the effective rule to merges, and on first sync hands this computer's existing rules to your account unchanged.

Pooled Claude tabs and Orchestrators now launch with MCP tool search on (`ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true`), so a session with many MCP tools defers their schemas instead of sending all of them on every request and auto-compacting into a thrash.

With the repository kickoff flag on, a kickoff on another of your machines (Runs on → Your machines, or Auto ranking one) starts there from the same repository list, and that machine uses its own copy of each repository or clones it. The scope line stays and adds "· <machine>'s copy". Auto follows the ranked machine when it has been updated and otherwise stays on This machine, naming it; picking an older machine with repositories asks you to update Terminal there. With the flag off nothing changes.

A live thread stream asks again after a home answers `thread_stream_unsupported`: a minute later, doubling to ten minutes, while the poll carries on, so a backend restart no longer ends live streaming for open chats.

Orchestrator threads now follow the order the project's Mac or cloud home recorded, on this Mac, on another Mac's project, in the cloud copy and on the web. A reply that is running when you send a message keeps its earlier text above it, and what comes later goes below. The Queued tray shows only the messages the Orchestrator has not read yet, and a message you sent shows one time: when it was read.
Avoid global process and open-file inventory for signed-out archive-only storage runs while preserving cleanup safety checks for other runs.
Run capacity and Turbo script checks before overlapping the remaining Terminal CI checks, preserving the full test inventory, one package deadline, failure reporting, and process cleanup.

The update popover now counts this computer, lists each of your computers with its version and state, and Update all restarts every ready computer at once (one still downloading installs as soon as it is ready) instead of leaving a busy computer waiting. "Restart this computer" is now "Update this computer".
Keep this computer's verified tunnel nickname visible while the machine list loads at startup.
Restart a failed Orchestrator on its home Mac when the person's message arrives, including through project sync.
Load handoff destinations without downloading the project's cloud copy, narrow Cloud VM rows to the project's connected repositories, and show progress while destinations load.

Settings → Agents → Repositories shows your organization's default rules and your own. Owners and admins edit the organization defaults; everyone else sees them read-only. Your rules sync to every computer, with account pins kept per computer, and a rule that differs from the organization default is marked. Project settings says when a rule is the organization's default.
Make all CodePress organizations coverage and MCP sign-in available without an organization rollout flag.
Detect agents launched through this tab's provider admission wrapper so Orchestrator messages, approvals, and agent paste submission work for running workers, including after a daemon update.

The Landed and Archived sections of the One feed rail keep their rows through every background refresh instead of flashing "Loading…". Pages you opened are read again only when the section's count changes, and the old rows stay on screen until the new ones arrive.

Show effective MCP access for authorized unclaimed offers in All organizations mode, keep project coverage labels tied to the stored flag, and refresh labels when the coverage mode changes, with compatibility for older backends.
Wait out lifecycle lock contention during worktree creation and restoration within the existing preparation wait bound.

Searching and filtering the One feed no longer sends a request and flashes a skeleton on every keystroke or click: the search is asked once typing pauses, and the rows already on screen stay (dimmed) until the new ones arrive. The Tabs kind no longer shows a skeleton at launch or on first visit, and an empty answer to a Landed or Archived refresh is retried once on the next refresh.

A new Synced project's card now reaches the cloud within seconds, even right after Terminal restarts, so a project started from another Mac opens there without a long wait. The card retries every 15 seconds at most, uploads ahead of other sync work, and the log says why when it has to wait.
Keep ordinary PR lookups to one GraphQL query, with lightweight discovery for fork collisions and bounded paging for larger evidence histories.

A project you start on another Mac from the kickoff still opens its thread here when its synced card arrives late. After the 30 second fast wait the kickoff keeps waiting for up to ten minutes and says "Still waiting for <machine> to sync it", and its notices no longer promise an automatic open once the wait has ended.

Focusing the Terminal window no longer flashes "Loading more…" in the project rail or re-reads it twice, and a failed Processes refresh keeps the last list on screen with a note instead of replacing it with an error.
Show Switching… on the account being selected while Terminal applies the login and reloads accounts, including computer-scoped selections and the tab subscription switcher.
The shared One feed rail gains an optional panel tab and its section headers move into their own file. Terminal passes no panel tab, so its rail looks and behaves as before.
Keep a new Orchestrator project's opening brief above the merge-authority and prompt-approval notices, and move briefs already written below them back to the top.

A launch with the one feed on no longer flashes today's rail and the Cloud label before the feed, and an open chat is no longer replaced by the empty New chat composer when the same account signs in again. The cached feed answer survives the account's auth generation moving, the open chat, searches and last painted thread follow the user and organization instead of the sign-in lineage, the menu bar is told the frontend is ready once, and the daemon log records when the generation moves.
Clear checkout-discovery state when resetting shared PR-status E2E fixtures.
Keep Terminal test transform caches separate across pnpm dependency store layouts.

List every banked subscription reset with its expiry and let each account use the chosen reset.
Gate Claude grants individually and start a new reset attempt after a definite provider outcome while preserving request IDs for ambiguous retries.

Terminal's one-feed rail gains an Automations tab after the kinds, replacing the top-row Automations button. It lists the organization's automations, with a count of those that need you, and opens a row, the overview or the create flow on the web page in Web mode. Offline it says "Automations need a connection".
The CI script that restores Terminal's Vitest module cache loads again where only the root dependencies are installed: it reads pnpm's install manifest with yaml only when it needs to.

A synced project's cloud copy now carries the same health and reason the home's rail and Home show, and it is re-sent when health changes with no other event (the quiet window passing, a limit wait ending), so other devices stop reading a stopped Orchestrator as a question waiting on you.
Show one New Cloud VM choice for project hand-off, with a repository picker when needed, and list recent owned computers with reasons when unavailable.
Keep current and asleep Macs correctly named in handoff pickers and show the update reason for unsupported online Macs.
Batch background CI-passed checks by repository through GraphQL, complete large heads with bounded paging, and retain urgent REST confirmation before delivery or Orchestrator success routing.
The left rail keeps its scroll position when you open a project, a cloud chat or New chat.
Add the Orchestrator folder to file roots and relative opens, with pane relay actions to resolve paths and names and search files.
Enforce synced Personal and Team repository restrictions across Terminal selection and failover, and expose a Repositories editor on account cards.
Let a person continue a rule-bound Claude or Codex agent on a healthy account after its subscription limit, with a composer limit strip and a temporary account bypass.
Open file references from another machine's live Orchestrator threads in Files, with remote content, line navigation, and inline compatibility notices.

Check repository access before handing off a project, reuse the receiver's own checkout, and report checkout failures without importing an empty folder.

Keep checked repository identities stable through source stop and refuse occupied managed checkout paths with a different GitHub origin.

Refuse captured or retried payloads that introduce repositories outside the receiver's checked manifest.

Apply the same check before receiver checkout preparation for older senders and parked restores.
Continue a limited, rule-bound Orchestrator on another healthy account from the strip above its composer, until the bound account resets.
Make Orchestrator file search visible in Files and the thread header, and open it with the keyboard shortcut from every view, including live synced copies and unavailable hosts with an explanation.
Add an opt-in redacted authorization observer for remote-control daemon diagnostics while preserving normal authorization and deadlines.
Show MCP sign-in cards in Orchestrator projects and chats and notify the Orchestrator when sign-in completes or fails.
Link existing bare file names and relative paths in Orchestrator prose, opening the resolved file in Files. Guide project and chat replies to write file mentions as links.
Orchestrator rail: switching between the kind tabs and the Automations tab no longer moves the tab row, the filter row or the first section header.
Keep the Accounts computer sheet above the iOS app's floating bottom bar, with safe-area padding and two-line phone summaries.
Keep the Accounts settings panel, scope filters, organization selector and account cards inside a phone viewport, with centered Settings tabs and compact outlined actions.

Cloud mode: opening the Apps page or an App no longer opens a system-browser tab for each App iframe or for frames inside a migrated Framer site. Links you click to other sites still open in your browser, and the CodePress sign-in is now written only into CodePress's own web pages.
Orchestrator rail: clicking an automation in the Automations tab now shows it beside the rail instead of switching the window to Web mode. Open full page still goes to the web page.
Throttle the Orchestrator's push-driven cloud feed reads to one per 2 seconds, and let a pushed narrowed read share an unfiltered cloud read already in flight instead of starting another.

A local Orchestrator project or chat no longer raises the "Sign in to your MCP servers" question by itself. It appears only when the Orchestrator calls `request_mcp_sign_in` for a server its current work needs, so a new project no longer lands in Needs you for a sign-in nobody asked for. Sign-in stays available in Settings → Agent MCPs.
Explain why CodePress organization coverage must be changed in that computer's own Terminal, disable the control in connected remote windows, and keep refused saves visible in Settings.

Record a rule-bound Orchestrator's launch repository before pinning a restricted subscription account, and explain refusals using the project setting or repository rule and the account's allowed repositories.
Saving a project's state on another device no longer re-reads the Orchestrator rail and feed; only a card change does.

The Orchestrator's MCP sign-in card has Don't ask again on each server, kept per computer and listed under Settings → Agent MCPs → Muted sign-in prompts with Unmute. The card no longer lists a server your Orchestrator already reports as connected, and shows servers on the same host as one row.
Keep failed attachments from being omitted by cloud agent chat sends, while preserving the Orchestrator composer's text-send behavior.
Carry a Team-pinned tab's repository through the relay so restricted Team accounts work in their allowed repositories, with tokens cached separately per repository.
Restore interrupted GitHub stats collection locally from an exact canonical copy before acknowledging, avoiding repeated snapshot downloads.
Return 404 for reserved preview hostnames on the Terminal control listener before HTTP or WebSocket admission.
Recover invalid retained GitHub stats canonical data by downloading the complete published snapshot after local restoration rolls back.
Add suspendable worktree cleanup leases with durable per-path cleaning fences and log lifecycle locks still held after ten seconds.
Typing in the One feed search redraws only the rail instead of the whole Orchestrator view; the feed hears the search once typing pauses.
Boot capacity-host Kata VMs at their admitted CPU and memory size, reserving guest overhead within the memory limit.
Find text with Cmd/Ctrl+F in the Orchestrator prompt editor and keep Contents on the section visible while scrolling.
Show temporary shared GitHub stats server congestion as busy, retaining cached ranges without marking the server offline.
Feed rows leave the rail the moment you archive, delete or mark them handled, and come back with the error notice if the write is refused.

Add "Land project…" to the ⋯ menu of a local building project in the Projects rail and the one-feed rail. The dialog lists the work items that aren't done, and landing cancels them with a reason the landed summary records.

Release the worktree lifecycle lock before settled-worker cleanup waits, abandon stale pending quits, back off retained tabs and merged rows, and settle PTY-only cleanup after recorded processes exit.
Let owners turn on remote unlock for a locked Mac from another signed-in device, with a host notification and audit event.

Archiving a project answers as soon as the archive is saved; closing its session and removing its worktrees now finish in the background, retried if a folder is kept, with a rail notice pointing to Settings → Storage when something could not be removed.

Isolate local Browser Tab previews from Terminal controls, strip Terminal credentials from preview relays, and preserve old preview links with safe navigation redirects. Preview applications start with fresh browser storage once. Linux uses dedicated loopback preview listeners.

A quiet strip above the composer says how many MCP servers need sign-in and fades after a few seconds, and a key chip with the count stays in the composer toolbar. Its list has Sign in and Ignore for each server. When your Orchestrator asks you to sign in to specific servers, the question names them and says why.
While a One feed search is pending, the rail narrows the rows it already holds by title instead of dimming them all, and says "Searching…" when none match; the cloud answer replaces it.
Add the default-off `useUnifiedShell` gate for the unified shell. Nothing reads it yet.
Label headless Claude sessions as codepress while preserving ambient authentication.
Make This Mac handoff previews probe only the home Mac, check handoff targets concurrently, and show loading, retry, and Needs update states in the picker.
Reconnect enrolled machines after a device-channel sign-in timeout and include the reason when a channel stops.
Show online machines with green dots and unavailable machines and suspended cloud VMs with outline moons in the Machines menu, preserving retry indicators.
Show one notice in the @ menu when this machine cannot make cross-machine reads, instead of blaming each online machine's discovery.
Show Claude accounts' Fable and other per-model weekly usage in Accounts without changing account availability or selection.
Land project… is also in the ⋯ menu of a building cloud project, and landing refuses (and shows the new list) when the project's unfinished work items changed after the dialog opened.

Send each local project's page list to CodePress so its shared plan canvas matches Terminal. The list goes after every plan publish and page removal, and once at start for projects whose list changed, at most one send per project at a time; a failed, slow or unsupported send never fails the publish and is retried on the next change or start. The Orchestrator is told the plan page's share link opens every page once there are two or more, when CodePress has taken the list.

Open Project settings inside the Details panel so the conversation and composer stay available. Settings fit narrow panels and the phone drawer, with Back, Esc and the settings icon returning to Work or Plan.

Enable narrow worktree creation locking by default and retain the explicit false fallback. Fence a reused physical checkout before hydration, and let worker relaunch wait out lifecycle lock holders while releasing the lock before agent launch or slow failed-tab disposal.
Show the offline moon for shared machines even when their inline connection failed.
Keep headless device channels retrying after machine-auth refusals, while preserving hard stops for revoked machines.

Keep worker cleanup's slow probes, snapshots and quarantine deletion outside the machine-wide worktree lock while a per-path cleaning marker protects the original checkout. Revalidate ownership before moving and recording, and preserve changed quarantine copies for recovery.
Open and save files outside a project's folders on its home machine from a remote Terminal or web thread, with the same private-data refusal as the home opener.
Hydrate shared GitHub stats in larger snapshot pages, with a 100-row compatibility fallback for older backends.
Update the Claude Agent SDK to 0.3.312, shipping Claude Code 2.1.312 for local Orchestrator and local-device agent sessions. Existing sessions keep their conversation history when resumed.
Show bounded device-channel and remote-control reasons in headless status, and recovery hints for running machines with a disconnected control channel.

Allow slow capacity hosts up to 90 seconds to connect to the Kata guest agent,
with a longer host boot-command timeout. Hosts adopt the change after updating
the CLI and running host leave followed by host join.

Show the Orchestrator's HTML plan pages again on the Overview tab. The desktop app's local-control origin guard was refusing the plan page frame with `ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`; it now admits that frame's page load, as it already does for file and media frames.
Make cross-machine chat mentions always available in the composer and kickoff, while preserving ownership, organization and receiver capability checks.
Show the last-known Accounts snapshot immediately while refreshing in the background, and remove unnecessary computer polling and duplicate account reads.

Hydrate missing account preferences, engine policy and subscription status on the first Terminal settings read within a shared three-second deadline, then return cached settings during background refreshes. Serve recent Team credential status during refresh.

Answer a project delete as soon as its agents and Orchestrator are stopped and the project is deleted; closing the workers' tabs and removing their worktrees and the project folder continue in the background, and the delete preview reads workers in parallel.
Make Remote unlock setup visible in Remote Access settings and onboarding, and preset never-chosen lock-screen access when Desktop hosting is turned on.
Treat projects that moved away as remote in Hand off so This Mac can bring them back without offering their current home as a destination.
Release the machine-wide worktree lock during storage cleanup, folder and session reclaim, and workflow removal so unrelated worktrees can launch while cleanup runs.

Removing a worker's folder waits for a closed tab's exit instead of polling for it, a project's trees share one process read, archive releases a project's repository trees in parallel, and each removal logs how long every step took.

Continue limited Terminal workers through sponsored subscriptions on the hosted relay and show read-only sponsor availability in Accounts. Preserve newer project account choices during sponsored replacement startup.

Settings → Storage now shows why a project folder was left on disk even when its path is long: the reason leads and the whole removal command follows, instead of the command's two long paths cutting the reason off.
Re-home live synced projects after a Terminal device-id change when their prior home is offline and the local replica generation still matches.
Install shared GitHub stats snapshots with reusable bulk SQLite writes, preserving atomic recovery and reporting lease loss before collection continues.
When another device changes a synced project, the sidebar now updates that row in place instead of re-reading the whole feed, so a project that needs you moves to Needs you within a moment.

With the organization's unified shell flag on, the main window draws an icon rail in place of the title bar's Agent / Apps / Terminal switcher. Agent and Terminal keep their warm layers, every other section opens its page inside the shell, Automations lists the organization's automations beside the page, and ⌃1–⌃9 (Alt+1–9 off macOS) move between sections. The window opens as before with the flag off.

With the unified shell on, the rail's section shortcuts (⌃1–⌃9, Alt+1–9 off macOS) are Settings → Keybindings rows ("Go to Terminal section" and so on) that can be rebound or cleared, match the physical digit key on any keyboard layout, and take Alt+digit from terminal programs only while the shell is drawn. Moving the pointer along the rail no longer blanks the embedded page, and a chat link that falls back to the web view no longer lights the wrong rail entry.
Label worker-cleanup lock holders and report locked setup time to identify repeated cleanup contention.
Finish handoffs to a Mac that already holds the project, report target-side failures, and offer recovery when a handoff is still waiting.
Pace terminal WebSocket bulk replay and sessions broadcasts on socket backpressure, serialize replays per connection, and log every socket close.
Reuse stamped checkout identities when routing PR events, avoiding repeated branch and origin Git processes across unchanged Terminal tabs while detecting checkout and remote changes.

With the organization's unified shell flag on, Settings is one section of the rail instead of a dialog. Its list holds Account (Preferences), Organization (General, Integrations, Platform MCP, Members, Teams, Navigation and the admin pages), which open the same web pages as the dashboard, and This machine, which holds this computer's tabs: General, Keybindings, File Viewer, Agents, MCPs, Orchestrator, Voice, Computers, Network, Usage, Storage and GitHub Stats. The gear and ⌘, open This machine; with the flag off they open the dialog as before.
Bound and share Hand off destination discovery, preserve live Mac presence during slow probes, and log transfer stage timings.
Show Reconnecting while the machine still answers health probes, retaining accepted agent counts until their receipt lease expires on desktop and phone.
Flatten Agents Accounts into compact expandable rows with a simpler computer toolbar and actionable provider readiness.

Isolate remote Browser Tab apps on the machine's preview host, with single-use
bootstrap tickets and an opaque sandbox fallback when that host is unavailable.
Limit fallback resource grants to their issuing port and scheme, with short
expiry and renewal authenticated by the open Browser Tab's control page.
Restrict remote-machine native commands to their window's control origin.
Group Hand off destinations into compact lists, show the route beneath the selected destination, and use shared timed progress and recovery views on desktop and phones.

With the unified shell flag on, the status bar is gone and everything it did moves into the rail's machine picker: the tunnel URL (copy, edit, QR code), Processes, the agent scope, the update and restart pills, queued-message delivery, Software Factory activation, the agent dashboard toggle, reconnect, "Open another computer…" (the machines menu) and "Connect a computer…". The computer you are driving remotely and notices such as a pending key prefix or other viewers show on the picker button with the menu closed. Choosing a machine in the picker marks it as the selected one in the menu; the rows still act on this computer. With the flag off the status bar is unchanged.
A chat's change reaches the feed on screen as one pushed row, and a chat whose card is gone is removed by its row key, with no feed read.

Keep remote windows connected during large post-connect output bursts by treating every inbound frame as liveness, while retaining a separate pong deadline and reporting heartbeat close reasons and round-trip timing.

Probe immediately on foreground return and share a three-second, any-frame focus probe across desktop, browser and remote-machine windows.

Retry unconfirmed pool-host VM cleanup while online, escalate ineffective guest kills only to verified owned processes, recover transient preflight failures, report redacted cleanup errors, and bound host leave with a configurable timeout (600 seconds by default).

With the organization's unified shell flag on, My Work, Servers and Media are drawn by Terminal itself in the shell's page instead of loading codepress.dev in the embedded webview. My Work's Coordination and Done tabs each have their own address, so a Done pick survives leaving and coming back. A conversation link opens in the Agent layer, and Create MicroVM still opens the embedded Servers page. Apps, Design and Automations are unchanged, and so is the window with the flag off.
Add a strict authenticated owner UI request predicate for future daemon routes and verify the Terminal UI origin boundary.

The Agent (Orchestrator) mode button no longer disappears from the title bar when the account has not loaded; the mode shows its loading or sign-in state instead, and a failed account read after a window reload is retried.

Ghostty tabs now render incrementally from libghostty's dirty render state, at most once per display frame, and stop rendering while hidden. A busy background Ghostty tab no longer pins the UI thread and lags typing in other tabs.
Let owners change CodePress organization coverage and launch-at-login settings from a connected Terminal window on another computer, with owner UI authentication and clear save errors.

Ghostty terminal tabs now encode keys with Ghostty's own mode-aware encoder, so Esc, Ctrl+[ and Ctrl+] work in nvim (including when it enables the kitty keyboard protocol), and paste, focus reports, Ctrl+Shift+C/V, macOS Option and Cmd editing keys, IME input, scrollback shortcuts and the # mention picker behave as they do in xterm tabs.

Ghostty tabs whose broker died (for example after a Linux restart) now come back as a fresh shell with their agent resumed, as Ghostty when the runtime verifies and as xterm otherwise, instead of sitting on "Ghostty has not attached this tab yet" forever. The PTY broker no longer panics on SIGTERM after its Ghostty worker exits, a recovering model no longer rejects a new attach outright, and every attach rejection is now logged with the step that refused it.
Record how long each launch step takes, from daemon start to the first rows in the rail, and report it in `get_terminal_diagnostics`.
Show the home's full Project settings on synced copies, with instruction Restore and implementation model Reset controls when the home supports them.
Opening the Landed or Archived section of the Orchestrator rail now shows skeleton rows while its projects load, instead of "Loading…" text.

Terminal's native My Work, Servers and Media pages follow Terminal's theme in dark and light, Media thumbnails load from the media CDN, and My Work shows an error with Try again instead of endless loading rows.
The Orchestrator rail now shows the Archived count as a plain number: it is no longer drawn with a "+" when a project list was cut, because the count now covers every archived project.

The daemon starts accepting requests sooner on launch: it no longer opens the Orchestrator store, reconciles file saves or starts the usage ledger before it listens, and restores sessions beside the account pools instead of behind them. A file save during the first moments answers a retryable "starting" and goes through once ready.

An Orchestrator worker waiting between turns on an open pull request now reads "Waiting on checks for #42 · last: pushed a commit" (or QA, the judge, "Ready to merge") instead of "Idle after: ran ls", and the idle line skips reads and look-around commands.
The unified shell's icon rail shows the CodePress logo at the top, or your organization's own logo when it has uploaded one; pressing it opens Agent.

Orchestrator: once a work item's pull request is open, its phase no longer goes back to Coding. The pull request's own updates stop resetting the item to "In checks", a write that sets `implement` on an item with an open pull request is stored as checks, and a judge FAIL shows "fixing judge findings · round N" while the item stays in review. The 3-hour step check now calls the Verify step Review.

Allow an Orchestrator outside a git repository to use a restricted account when every recorded project repository is covered, consistently across window and host launches and the account picker. Explain uncovered repositories in refusal messages.
Signed-in daemons listen sooner: the device channel starts right after the daemon listens instead of opening the Orchestrator store first.
Keep lock-screen unlock off in permission onboarding unless the person enables it, preserving existing saved choices.

A work item's card reads Code, Review, Ready, Merged, and stays "In review" from the pull request opening until it is Ready or Merged, whatever the worker is doing. The Work tab groups items by their own step, and the project track is Brief, Plan, Build and Land, with Build showing how many items are in review.
Address direct project handoffs back to This Mac by the home's device id and reuse its account-fenced machine inventory for preview and start.
Keep owned Macs in Hand off destinations when device presence or tunnel probes are slow, with account-scoped last-good presence and disabled asleep fallbacks.

The rail's feed rows arrive sooner at launch: the daemon starts the first feed read itself once it is listening, the feed setting and the cloud read are asked at the same time, the answer no longer waits for the Landed lookup's later pages, and the rail asks again the moment the daemon is ready instead of on a timer.

The unified shell now follows each person's own "Unified shell" switch in the web app's Feature Flags menu instead of an organization setting. It is off until you turn it on, and Terminal picks the change up within a minute.

The feed's rows now carry the facts the filters compare (a chat's source and agent key), and this Mac's own chats, projects and agent tabs set them, so the rail can apply the server's filter rules to rows it already holds.
Release the worktree lifecycle lock during Orchestrator session and further repository refreshes while keeping their preparation fences and honoring the existing wide-lock opt-out.
Keep account-switch errors on their owning Personal or Team card, and prevent background choice refreshes from superseding a single explicit account switch.

A message to a landed project now restarts its Orchestrator conversation whichever surface sent it (the web, another Mac or a synced copy, not only this Mac's composer), a paused project still holds it until resumed, and a turn that cannot start says why in the thread and answers once the cause clears.

A landed project's Orchestrator conversation keeps the build's context: each Orchestrator session records where its provider ran, and a landed conversation that cannot resume starts from the landing summary and the newest thread entries instead of a single line. A project handoff now carries the transcript of a build that ran in its session worktree.

Launch asks for each thing once: the agent-feed setting, the organization list and the dock badge's count share one request each, the classic project list reads only this Mac's projects while the agent feed is healthy, and Automations load beside the feed instead of after it.

Fix pool-host VM cleanup on real hosts: command timeouts derived from the monotonic clock are now whole milliseconds, so destroy no longer fails with "Invalid host command timeout" before it can stop or remove a sandbox.

Ticking a filter in the feed rail now shows the matching rows you already have right away, with an "Updating…" bar, instead of dimming the list; an asleep machine in the filter menu no longer looks disabled.

Terminal launches faster on a large Orchestrator store: a store the last open already migrated skips the schema checks and one-time backfills instead of repeating them every boot. The first launch after updating still runs them once.
Retry orphaned pool sandboxes and failed canary cleanup while the host stays online, allowing qualification to recover without a reconnect.
Keep background desktop windows connected while their timers are suspended, and probe the live connection briefly on return before reconnecting.
Let synced project copies choose the home's subscription accounts and browse and change its Project folder with the home's validation.

Turn on concurrent background Computer Use by default while preserving saved opt-outs. Background leases on non-overlapping windows can run together; overlapping targets and foreground input keep their existing serialization.
Run host doctor's local canary only when the host service control socket is absent or refuses the connection. Report other service errors without starting a second canary.
Start and control ready lock-screen Desktop sessions through the native bridge so a throttled Mac app window does not block remote unlock.

Orchestrator project stores already opened by a recent build run the schema pass once more, so they get the `settings_revision` column that synced copies need to change home accounts and project folders.
Let the local Orchestrator mark reviewed pull requests ready without merge authority or approval, while keeping merge approval requirements.

An Orchestrator or any agent can now message a landed project: `message_orchestrator`, Terminal `send_message` and `list_orchestrators` treat it like any stopped project. The message is kept and wakes it, starting or resuming its landed conversation, within the existing 6-wakes-per-10-minutes limit per sender. A landed start that was refused before it began is retried when its cause clears, without another send, at doubling gaps up to 10 minutes.

With the unified shell on, pressing Apps, Design, Automations or Evals loads the page once and leaves it: the embedded page no longer draws the header layout before the headerless one, a section pressed again is not reloaded when the webview reports its own spelling of the address, and Automations no longer redirects off its section.
Report a successful handoff to This Mac when the home Mac's start reply is lost, and follow the same move on Retry.

The rail draws what it last showed the moment Terminal launches, then updates to live without jumping: unchanged rows stay put, changed rows update in place, moved rows slide, and the list holds your place. Chats, projects and automations are remembered on this Mac only.

The inbox poll's scan for landed projects that are waiting on a message now narrows them with one query first, so a Mac with hundreds of landed projects no longer runs the per-project checks for every one of them on every poll.
Let GitHub stats finish loading while shared collection publishes new snapshots, coalescing background refreshes without cancelling the current request.

With the unified shell on, switching between Apps, Design, Automations and Evals routes inside the page that is already loaded instead of loading the whole web app again, so a later switch no longer repeats the sign-in, organization and settings reads. A web page that cannot route itself, or a page on another origin, is loaded as before.

Add GPT-6.1 Terra usage rates and pin the stable Codex SDK and CLI to 0.165.0, with authenticated native role/follow-up and interruption captures. Restricted assessment/design profiles accept the native apply_patch advertisement under the owner's release decision.

Hand a project off to a new Cloud VM reliably: a VM the backend reports ready but whose Terminal is not yet answering, or whose Orchestrator host is still starting, now shows as "waiting for the destination" instead of failing with "Destination is not the claimed VM" or "The VM image is missing the running Orchestrator host capability". A project also moves in any state: an Orchestrator still mid-turn after a 20-second grace is stopped (its turn settles interrupted and the destination resumes it) instead of the handoff failing with "The PM is still running a turn".
Show the exact local expiry time for every usage reset in Accounts.
A project that finished moving to another machine can now be archived and deleted from its ⋯ menu on the old machine, instead of being refused with "finish or cancel the transfer".
Remove feed rail refresh indicators and their reserved space, and add floating previous/next section buttons that respect reduced motion.
Let handoff previews proceed when a Mac's availability checks time out, while still blocking confirmed offline Macs.
Feed rail: archiving or deleting another machine's project or chat moves the row into Archived or removes it at once, and a saved agent tab's ⋯ offers Forget saved copy….

Capture bounded pool session runner output and expose redacted tails on exit and in host status.
Restrict status tails to the root control socket and keep draining guest output when capture storage fails.
Restore the update badge on the unified shell's machine picker when an update needs attention.
Keep landed projects from showing worker-wait activity and refresh saved landing context on follow-up conversation turns.

Open after moving a project to a New Cloud VM now opens that VM through its viewer grant, the handoff destination list no longer shows a Cloud VM as an offline "localhost" Mac, and a Cloud VM page opened without a viewer grant says how to open it instead of asking for a reload.
Parked Cloud VMs can be terminated from their card and detail view, discarding their saved work.
Refuse capacity-host qualification when all configured slots cannot fit the live data disk or memory, crediting resources held by running sandboxes and reporting actionable capacity reasons.

A shared computer now passes a teammate's live project reads and messages from their other devices to that teammate's own Orchestrator. It advertises `actor_orchestrator_live: 1`, beside the unchanged `actor_orchestrator: 1`, so the backend can tell it supports them.
A Cloud VM viewer opened while the VM is parking now says so ("This cloud VM is parking. Reopen it from your machine list later.") instead of reconnecting forever.
Starting a project on a computer a teammate shared now opens its thread in this window, as a project started on one of your own machines does, when synced cards are on for the organization.

A Cloud VM park that fails now logs the failing step, the HTTP status and the backend's reason, and reports a specific `park_error` such as `release_refused_400` in place of `park_failed`. A refused release is still retried on the next heartbeat, so a backend fix completes a stuck park without restarting the guest, and the park's failure summary is logged once per new error code rather than every heartbeat.

Free capacity-host slots after a definite VM boot failure when successful task and process inventories confirm that no task, shim or hypervisor remains. Preserve pending cleanup retry backoff across reconciliation and stop requests.

Size pool host CPU defaults from available cores, reserve one core per slot for VM overhead, reject oversubscribed hosts in doctor, and show host sizing in status.

Existing hosts retain their saved CPU budgets and can become Not ready under the stricter reserve check. To resize, run `host drain --wait`, then `host leave` and `host join` with lower `--slots` or `--cpu-millicores`; omit the CPU flag to use the new default. Rejoin requires a fresh install token or a new device-code approval.
A launch-recovery ask for a worker that never started no longer opens once its work item is done or cancelled; its history reads as retired by the platform.
Add an in-memory component-test harness for Terminal screens and move two mocked Network Access settings checks out of the browser suite.
Free a capacity-host slot after a returned VM boot failure only when repeated task and process inventories confirm absence; include redacted offline leave cleanup errors.

Hand off… on a cloud project in Orchestrator mode: the thread header and the feed row's ⋯ open a picker that lists this Mac first, then your other Macs, then Cloud once the Orchestrator is on a Mac, and moves only the Orchestrator there. The run-location tag then names the Mac it runs on.
Show the update pill at the top right of the Terminal title bar, so a pending update is visible with the machine menu closed, and remove the update entry from the left machine menu.

Workers the Orchestrator launches (`project_fleet_assign`, `project_worker_relaunch`) now get the same managed computer-use binding as an agent started from a Terminal tab, so Claude and Codex workers list `computer_execute` and `computer_reset` when computer use is on. If the binding cannot be made, the worker still starts and its `mcp_servers` row reports `computer_use_unbound` instead of an empty tool list.

The Orchestrator can retire a launch-recovery ask itself, with a recorded reason, when it recovered a failed launch some way other than a relaunch, so the person is no longer left a restart decision for work that is already done.

Native computer-use failures are easier to diagnose: a refused bridge request now reports the closed route and HTTP status class (`bridge_rejected`/`lease_lost`, never the body) instead of `unknown`, and a foreground `stale_handle` says which freshness check failed. Codes, effects and authority are unchanged and nothing is replayed.
Reuse unchanged local E2E server builds and lane-specific web bundles, with forced rebuild and web dev-server opt-outs.

Recover the owned browser after a stale CDP session or a failed computer-use reset. A browser tool call that hits a dead tab session now returns a short refusal without replaying anything, closes the original tab, and opens a fresh one on the next call. A computer-use reset that ended in error can be retried with `retryCleanup` and settles at the same generation once the original tab is confirmed closed.

With the unified shell on, pressing Apps, Design, Automations, Evals, Integrations or Settings from Agent, Terminal or one of the shell's own pages no longer flashes the page the embedded view was left on first: the view stays hidden until the page you pressed has painted, or a short timeout has passed. Resting the pointer on a rail button over an embedded page no longer blanks it, since no tooltip is drawn over the embedded page.

The pages Terminal draws itself in the unified shell can now read the signed-in person, the page's query and title, in-app confirm and prompt dialogs, file uploads and host-supplied pieces from Terminal, ready for Evals, Automations and the Apps list to move in. Nothing changes on screen yet.

A Mac that receives an Orchestrator handed off from the cloud no longer needs the project's repository checked out first: Terminal reuses its checkout of that repository or clones one, starts the Orchestrator there, and tells CodePress which folder it used.
Retire Cloud VM launch and handoff destinations while preserving parked-work recovery and handoff to this Mac.

Add `sign_in_to_codepress` to the local browser: an agent can open CodePress in its browser already signed in as the account Terminal is signed in to, instead of asking you to log in. Signing out of Terminal, letting the login expire or switching accounts also clears that browser's CodePress login.
Pass each Codex worker's project TMPDIR to its threads on the shared daemon, and direct worker scratch and QA evidence into that folder.

Hand off now offers every one of your online Macs for a cloud project's Orchestrator. A Mac without a checkout of the project's repository reads "Will check out owner/repo" and checks it out when it takes over.

Native computer-use failures name their real cause to the guest: an adapter failure thrown after the host replied now reports `fence_not_quiescent`, `receipt_mismatch` or `terminal_not_quiescent` with the `settle` phase instead of `unknown`, an adapter failure thrown while acquiring a lease names its code and fixed sentence in `errorDetail` (a mismatched lease reply is `lease_mismatch`), a foreground input refused because its target window is not focused says so instead of "Native step could not complete", and a malformed native action argument (for example an object passed to `listWindows`) ends as `invalid_input` with no effect and no reset when nothing was admitted. The one code change is that a malformed argument is now `invalid_input` instead of `adapter_error`; every other code, all effects and authority are unchanged and nothing is replayed.

A project moved to a new Cloud VM no longer fails with "Sign in to GitHub CLI" while the VM's GitHub credential is still coming up (the move now waits), and the VM is no longer parked 15 minutes after the project arrives.

Select a Personal Claude or Codex account that shares its email with a Local sign-in or another Personal one but belongs to a different workspace; it is filed as `personal-<id>` instead of failing with "cannot be distinguished", and a Claude reconnect must sign in to the same organization.

With the unified shell on, Evals (the suites list, a suite and its tabs, run comparison and the new-eval form) is drawn by Terminal itself in the shell's page instead of loading codepress.dev in the embedded webview. Leaving Evals for Agent or another section and coming back keeps the open suite and tab and a half-typed new eval, and a link to a suite opens it in Terminal. Apps, Design and Automations are unchanged, and so is the window with the unified shell off.

When two sign-ins are the same account (or Terminal can't tell them apart yet), Settings → Accounts now says what is wrong and offers the fix — Use Local account, Move Local to Personal, Use the other one, Reconnect or Remove from this computer — instead of "Try again". Rows show the problem before you click, the All computers view offers the same actions, and a Claude sign-in moved or reconnected to Personal now sends its organization.

Handing a project off from a Mac on an older Terminal no longer fails with "The bundle must carry rows for project_previous_landings": a table added after the bundle format shipped imports as empty when the sender predates it. When the destination does refuse a project copy, the source Mac now resumes the project's Orchestrator and workers at once instead of leaving it read-only until Resume here.
Landed and Archived in the Orchestrator rail now show visible, row-sized placeholders while their first page loads, in every theme.

Hand off… on a project whose last transfer already finished now opens the destination chooser again instead of replaying that transfer's "Handed off" result. A project handed off to a computer that has since gone quiet can be taken back with Continue here.

Project hand-off now finds the Orchestrator's CLI on a destination the same way agent launches do (through the login shell's PATH), and the move dialog shows the home Mac's own refusal message instead of raw JSON.

With the unified shell on, Settings → Organization → General, Members, Teams, Navigation, Quicklinks and Audit, and Account → Preferences, are drawn by Terminal itself instead of loading codepress.dev in the embedded webview, so pressing Settings opens General at once. A half-edited General form is still there after a visit to Agent, Members offers invitations by opening the web Members page, and Billing, Integrations and the other Organization pages stay in the embedded view (shown only after they have painted). The window with the unified shell off is unchanged.

A new hand-off of a project whose own earlier transfer failed while still holding the source claim now releases that failed transfer the way Resume here would, then moves. When that is not safe, it says why (the earlier move cannot be undone here, or its destination has not confirmed the cancel yet) instead of "Another project handoff already owns this source".

With the unified shell on, the Apps section's list (folders, apps and, for organizations with collections, the collections view) is drawn by Terminal itself in the shell's page instead of loading codepress.dev in the embedded webview. Leaving Apps for Agent or another section and coming back keeps the open folder or collection and what was typed in its search, and opening an app shows its page in the embedded view without first flashing the page it was left on. New app and Make a widget from a collection ask for the message in a small card, start the chat with the collection's instructions and open it in the Agent layer. Link a site, Add a blog and Migrate a site open the web's Apps page. Design and Automations are unchanged, and so is the window with the unified shell off.

Native computer use: a deliberate foreground step (`computer.native.foreground`) now reaches the native adapter as a foreground request, so the focus-then-click workflow is no longer refused as "unavailable in background delivery".

A background native click or key on a window that is already focused is now refused before any input as `unsupported` with effect none, instead of cancelling the lease and surfacing `terminal_not_quiescent` with an unknown effect.

A project handed off from this Mac now shows its synced copy once the transfer finishes, so you can keep reading and replying to it here instead of seeing a read-only tombstone. With no synced copy, the composer names the machine the project now runs on.

When the CodePress phone app opens a machine's live view from the shell's "Open on <Mac>", the Terminal page now focuses the tab the person came from. The page advertises `openTab` in its mobile-mode-ready message and answers `codepress:mobile-open-tab` by showing the Terminal and focusing that tab once the session list is live; a tab this machine does not have changes nothing. Older apps never send it, and the desktop window is unchanged.

The shared pages Terminal draws (My Work, Servers, Media, Evals) now carry phone-width layouts and bottom-sheet dialogs. Terminal's window is never phone width, so nothing changes on screen; the pages' dependency list gains two small modules.

The shared shell kit Terminal draws gains an optional "Open on <computer>" host capability. Terminal's own shell supplies none, so nothing changes in its window: the agent view, the machines list and saved tabs look and behave as before, except that an agent tab whose computer is away no longer draws a disabled message box.

Mac release builds now wait a few seconds for a busy disk image to release before giving up, and clean up an installer image an earlier build left mounted, so one stuck mount can no longer block every later Mac release.
Centre the phone home mode pill in one header and dock the kickoff composer above native navigation.

Shared Orchestrator thread code gains an opt-in phone header (title, panel button, ⋯ menu) and a soft-keyboard fold for the docked question. Terminal's own screens do not opt in, so nothing changes on screen here; the UI dependency closure is regenerated for the new file.
The shared shell's phone layout (not drawn in Terminal's own phone mode) swaps its bottom bar for a menu button and drawer.

Retire six default-on Terminal platform settings. Memory-aware fleet admission, bounded tab memory, Linux disk-staged updates, freeze sampling, the agent cursor, and signed Computer Use Driver hosting now run without their former toggles, including when older settings files contain false values.

Keep the focused Orchestrator kickoff input visible when the phone keyboard shrinks its scroller.
Use the singular "1 repo" in the compact prompt update notice.
Load one personal CodePress platform MCP catalog for local workers and the Orchestrator when Terminal supplies its broker, while preserving repository team access and the broker-skipped fallback.

Coalesce non-urgent Orchestrator inbox wakes, include PR head facts in notices, and keep actionable snapshot data ahead of history. Expose valid project post envelope states in the tool schema and validation errors.
Keep the Orchestrator PM on Opus while ordinary Anthropic chats default to Sonnet.

With the unified shell on, the Automations section (the activity overview, an automation and its run history, a run, its settings, the managed automations and the catalog) is drawn by Terminal itself in the shell's page instead of loading codepress.dev in the embedded webview. Selecting an automation in the list panel opens it in the page, and leaving Automations for Agent or another section and coming back keeps the open automation, its tab and run, and what was typed in its settings. A run's conversation opens in the Agent view on that session. The GitHub App controls of the managed automations stay on the web (the panel keeps its link to the GitHub settings), and starting a new automation still seeds the web's chat. The window with the unified shell off is unchanged.

Run the server tests that start agent sync, or that drain or count the whole fake clock, in their own process, so a timer another test leaves running cannot break them. Also keeps the Milkdown editor test independent of its packaged theme stylesheet and updates a stale expectation in the test selector. Test infrastructure only; no change to Terminal behavior.
