Keep visible kickoff fields in place when tapped, including oversized briefs during keyboard resize.

Terminal's new-chat screen now draws through shared new-chat pieces (layout, mode pill) that the web will reuse. Nothing changes on screen; the Chat | Orchestrator pill's test IDs are now `new-chat-mode*`.

Give Codex workers final-only native subagent reporting, longer waits, and bounded ordinary delegation with reserved QA capacity. Seed bridged Codex-home defaults only where the user has not set a value, preserving user choices and workspace trust.

The shared Audit, Quicklinks and Automations all-activity tables draw their rows as cards below the md breakpoint, so they never scroll sideways on a phone. Terminal's window is wider than that, so its tables are unchanged.

Fix native foreground `focus` and click on the installed host: the adapter compared the host's echoed target with the request's by key order, so every real foreground lease was refused as `lease_mismatch`. It now compares by value, and releases a lease the host admitted but the adapter refused so a reset can settle.

With the unified shell on, a link into another organization's My Work, Servers, Media, Evals, Apps, Settings or Automations page (a notification, a `codepress://open` link, a link in a chat, or a link a page builds) now opens in the embedded web view, where the web picks the organization from the link, instead of being drawn by Terminal under the organization it is on with the other organization's ids. Terminal does not switch organization for it, and the page you were on stays as you left it. A link to an organization you are not in no longer draws anything natively either. Links for the organization Terminal is on, and the window with the unified shell off, are unchanged.

New chat in Chat mode now shows the shared new-chat screen: the coloured "Hello, {name}!" greeting, four starter cards under the input, and Runs on in the row above the input (also in Orchestrator mode).
A project handed off from this Mac now opens as its synced copy when this Mac's cards arrive on the card stream, instead of the read-only tombstone.

The shared shell's phone layout gains a long press on a feed row that opens the row's menu as a bottom sheet, 44 px section-jump buttons, and a search button in the drawer when the host provides one (Terminal's own phone mode is unchanged).
Preserve checkpoint ownership when a retired cloud coding session resumes on a local runner.

Retire graduated Orchestrator rollout settings. Live replies, newest-first chats, pushed project cards, snapshot workers, stacked rail cards, weekly subscription usage, and the document workspace are always available; old stored opt-outs are ignored.
Document why Terminal and Factory operational environment switches are process-wide controls for the feature flag review; behavior and defaults are unchanged.
Prepare the desktop app to run from dependency layers kept outside the app bundle. Nothing changes until a release ships with layers.
Build each macOS architecture in its own release job so arm64 updates and the CLI publish without waiting for the Intel build.

Attribute verified native and proxy Claude requests to retained subscription
windows, with quota/reset history, bounded local HTTP/MCP reports and optional
provenance-preserving usage sync.
Show measured Claude subscription usage by retained five-hour and weekly window in Settings, with quota observations, separate source subtotals and explicit partial coverage.
Reduce server CI disk writes while assembling Terminal's PM SDK runtime, keeping release package copies independent.

Fix the Terminal unit test setup that made MilkdownEditor.test.tsx fail on the Blacksmith runners when the cached Vitest modules were restored: Vitest could not load a stylesheet from the pnpm store outside the checkout. No change to the app.
Restore Cloud VM handoff destinations for accounts in many organizations by scoping project reads to their organization and retaining account-bound Cloud discovery results after the picker deadline.

Let a page that draws its own phone header take the shell's header row and menu button, and let the Orchestrator screen use the shell's drawer instead of its own rail on a phone. Terminal's own layout is unchanged.
Add owner-authenticated live viewing and input transport for the visible browser handoff, with single-use tickets and a shared validated protocol.
Move the kickoff Chat | Orchestrator pill into the unified desktop shell's title bar, centred over the page column.

Settings tabs now tell a group heading, a setting's label and its description apart: headings are larger and bolder, descriptions smaller and muted, and a rule with more room separates one group from the next.
Keep Terminal's shared UI dependency manifest aligned with phone header slots and the shared slide-over primitives.
Draw Hand off… and Project settings as direct buttons in the phone Orchestrator thread's toolbar instead of behind a ⋯ menu.
Website and widget App cards on the Apps page now show their preview instead of a blank face: the window's content security policy lets them frame the App artifact gateway.

Terminal accepts an owner kickoff relayed by the backend (`owner_kickoff`) and starts the project in its owner's own Orchestrator, advertising `orchestrator_owner_kickoff` once Orchestrator messaging is ready.

On a shared computer, a teammate's New Tab, New Workflow and agent launches now open in their own session (created on first use) instead of failing, and the New Workflow dialog names their own subscription or CodePress's relay.

Teammates' Orchestrators and runs now start on a headless `codepress-terminal serve` host, which sets its app version itself. When one cannot start, the teammate sees one sentence naming the computer's owner, the computer and the fix, instead of the raw runtime error.
Servers, My Work and Media stay open while you are on another screen: coming back shows their rows at once and refreshes them in the background, and a hidden Servers page no longer polls.
Cloud mode now opens in a shared-computer window with your own CodePress sign-in, which stays on your machine and never reaches the shared computer.

Settings now looks like Slack's Preferences: a header with a close button, a grouped icon rail on the left and a titled pane on the right, and on a phone a full-screen list of sections that opens one at a time. Four sections are renamed: Terminal app, Agent MCPs, My computers and Local usage.

In a teammate's window on a shared computer, the Files panel now says the computer's files belong to its owner instead of failing to detect a project root, owner-only settings and entry points are hidden, and anything still refused says what it is and who can help instead of "Not available to teammates on this computer".
With the unified shell on, the top of the rail is now the current organization's tile (its logo, avatar or initials) and opens an organization switcher. The foot is the account menu.
The Automations list panel and the Automations page now share one summary read and poll, so Terminal's Automations tab no longer issues a duplicate `/summary` request while the page is open.
Open a waiting browser from its ask on your phone or another Mac, with live touch, keyboard and Paste controls. Browser WebSockets authenticate with a single-use owner ticket.

Shared computers: a teammate's window footer counts their own agents instead of reading "Agents unavailable". The computer owner's tabs, which an admin teammate can see, are badged as the owner's, dimmed and read-only, and the owner's output, input and attention text (such as their account errors) are kept from the teammate. The owner's settings gear is hidden in a teammate's window, and the session and worktree refusals name the owner when they are signed in.

With the Unified shell on, Settings opens as the same Slack-style modal as the dialog, grouped Account, Organization and This machine, over whatever section you were on, instead of a page in the list panel. Pages that live on the web, such as Billing, are marked with an external-link icon and close the modal to open in the web layer. Escape or the close button returns you to where you were.
Refuse retired live browser viewer actions after another daemon replaces the shared-profile handoff.

Repository kickoff now follows each person's own "Repository kickoff" switch in the web app's Feature Flags menu instead of an organization setting. It is off until you turn it on, and Terminal picks the change up within a minute: with it on, a new chat or Orchestrator project offers repositories instead of a Project folder.
The Chat | Orchestrator pill now slides its white thumb to the option you pick, with a short spring and a pop on the label, instead of swapping instantly.
Return live browser links from machine handoffs and guide agents to share them for human-only browser steps.
Add a Build panel setting under Settings → Orchestrator → Display (Last used, Open or Closed) that chooses whether a project's Work and Plan panel starts open in a wide window.

New workflows and new sessions now open their first tab in Ghostty when Ghostty is turned on, instead of always falling back to xterm. Every new terminal tab now goes through one shared admission step.
My Work, Media, Servers and Evals show the rows you last saw as soon as you open them, even after relaunching, then quietly update them from the server. Signing out deletes what was stored.
Pressing Design, Integrations or an App page now shows the page only once its content is on screen, and a page that reloads on its own no longer makes the next press wait out the timeout.

The unified shell's rail popups (organization switcher, account menu, machine picker, More) draw the theme's border colour instead of a white or black outline, with 12px corners, a shadow and small muted section labels, and open just past the rail. The current organization is marked by its check alone. Kit menus, selects, dialogs and sheets in Terminal also stop drawing their border in the text colour.
Publish a project's snapshot to its cloud copy as soon as it arrives on a Mac by direct move or takeover, so a later takeover never starts from the old home's copy.
Moving a project back onto a Mac that handed it off now goes through when the cloud still holds that Mac's own copy, continuing here at a generation the next direct move cannot collide with.
Settings → General now has a "Sessions and remote access" section with "Keep cloud copies of sessions" and "Remote agent actions". Organization admins can turn either off; members see them read-only.
Use the shared phone shell header for Orchestrator projects, with compact progress, the hosting machine and Work actions.
Show one "Picked up" line after a takeover, and share a running takeover between presses of the same project.
Ship seeded installers, a slim updater archive and separately signed dependency layers with every release, so a later update can download only what changed.

Apps and Automations show the rows you last saw as soon as you open them, even after relaunching, then quietly update them from the server. Each part of the page loads on its own, so it fills in as soon as its own answer arrives.

Settings calls the per-computer group "Computer · <name>" instead of "This machine", and the autocompact token contract and model catalog now come from the shared UI package so the web's Account → Agents page edits the same value with the same rules.

Subscription failover, PR readiness approval, review delivery, working hours, appearance and the agent automation toggles now follow your account across computers. Each Mac hands its own choices to your account once, the first time the account has none, and keeps them as its fallback; a change on one Mac reaches the others at their next refresh. New local Orchestrator projects start from your account's merge and prompt-approval defaults.
Update by downloading the slim app and only the dependency layers that changed, falling back to the full bundle on any failure.
A project that moved away from this Mac names where it went and can move again here or to a Cloud VM, including when that Mac is away and no cloud copy exists to continue from.
Mark retained MicroVM modules as deprecated so future agent work uses the ECS runner hosts.
Offer Hand off… on a project this Mac recorded as moved when sync is on, and add Continue here to the Moved banner.
Integrations is no longer its own rail entry: it is a row of Settings, and choosing it shows the web page beside the Settings list as Billing does.

After launch, My Work, Servers, Media, Evals, Apps and Automations quietly read their first page in the background, all at once, so the first press of each shows its rows with no loading skeleton. Nothing is read with Save-Data on, and a refresh that returns what is already shown no longer redraws the rows.

A chat or Orchestrator project started with repositories now opens worktrees off origin's default branch of Terminal's own managed clone (cloned the first time), never of a checkout of yours. A chat with repositories and no Project folder starts in the first repository's worktree. The remote kickoff's repository refusal now says the switch is yours.
Bundle the shared shell's pending-section state for phone drawer taps. Terminal draws no phone shell, so nothing changes on screen.

A stored page that no longer matches what the app expects can no longer break a section. Saved rows from a different app version are ignored and cleared, and a section that fails to draw saved rows clears them and loads again once.
The live terminal viewer for another machine's Orchestrator panes now runs on a shared stream client that can open any live terminal stream. Pane terminals look and behave as before.

Terminal can now stream any of its terminal tabs live, and open a new shell in a "Remote" session, for you on codepress.dev and the phone app. The web side ships in a later release. A new switch, Settings → Network → "Allow terminal from web & phone" (on by default), turns all of it off for this computer. The switch is also available as `allowRemoteTerminal` in `update_terminal_agent_settings`.

With the unified shell on, the Settings modal draws every section in its own pane, the web pages included (Integrations, Platform MCP, Team computers, Branding, Billing, Capacity, App hosting, Usage). Choosing one, or following a link to one, keeps the modal open; Escape, ⌘W and the close button return you to where you were.

Automations no longer reads the whole automation list again every time its activity summary refreshes. A running workflow's agent log now loads only its newest messages, and its step list leaves out the step inputs and outputs it never shows.

Settings → Account in Terminal draws the same Orchestrator, Agent accounts, Agents, Notifications and My computers pages as the web and the phone, in the shell's Settings modal and in the Settings dialog. The Computer tabs keep only what belongs to this computer: model defaults, the agent feed, the cloud copy, the step check, working hours, feature flags, compaction windows, the automation and pull-request switches, failover, keep-updated and each repository rule's merge choice now live on the Account page, and each leaves one line that opens it. The Computer group is named "Computer · <this computer>".
Add an extra Pinned section and Pin / Unpin actions for One-feed projects and chats, with cloud pins across computers and local offline mirrors.

A live terminal viewer on the web or the phone can fit the tab to its own window. It joins the tab's size like another window: the narrowest one wins, so while the Mac's window shows the tab it can only shrink it, and the tab gets its size back when the viewer lets go or leaves.
Folding the unified shell's list with ⌘\ now eases it shut and open over 200ms instead of snapping, and dragging the sidebar's resize handle follows the cursor without lagging behind it.

The Orchestrator's chat rail and Details panel now slide in and out over 200ms on desktop instead of snapping. The drawer terminal resizes once, at the final width, rather than on every frame of the slide.
Open a task handed off to the cloud in the Agent tab from its retained card.
Restore the Mac CLI publish, which refused every delivery because the ledger records a release ID only after the macOS lane completes.
Carry attachments and conversation mentions into projects started on your computer from the web or phone.
Hand a Terminal tab off to the agent runner from any organization: the Cloud destination no longer needs Coding VM Workspaces, and a task brought back into its tab keeps syncing.
A Cloud handoff the backend refuses now shows the backend's reason, such as the organization's concurrent session limit, instead of only a status code.
Let the Mac arm64 and Intel release builds run at the same time on one machine.
Linux releases build faster by restoring the Rust cache and skipping work on unchanged layers.
A Claude task brought back from Cloud into its tab keeps syncing to its cloud chat.
Track the shared phone viewport helper in Terminal's UI dependency closure.
Share Terminal's motion tokens and existing keyframes with codepress.dev while preserving Terminal's curves and timing.

Carry attachments and conversation mentions when starting projects on shared computers. Older computers receive signed file links and conversation references in the brief without blocking Send or showing a carry notice.
Make Work push the complete unified phone shell left with the shared phone panel animation, including the header and tabs.
Track the shared shell search field in Terminal's UI dependency closure so shared shell changes receive browser verification. Terminal's own search bar remains a separate change.
